Thiotepa and Belotecan, which are used in the treatment of these cancers, are also linked to Borderline Epithelial Tumor Of Ovary. This indicates that Gemcitabine may be repurposed for the treatment of Borderline Epithelial Tumor Of Ovary through a chain of drug-indication relationships. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the final scores reflect a probabilistic assessment of the relationship, and the pathways are indirect. The mechanisms underlying these associations are not fully understood, but they suggest a possible role of Gemcitabine in the treatment of certain epithelial tumors, though further research is needed to confirm its efficacy and safety in this context.
